A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CAP-TTA study. Their complete main texts and Appendices A–Q, including equations, tables and image-based figures, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original OOD-detection experiments, narrative-generation comparisons, ablations and human evaluations, including Tables 2–5 and 10.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results and reports revised human-agreement results in Table 10.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 changes the loss on concatenated history and safe text from explicitly conditional to unconditional probability, while Section 3.2 retains the conditional objective. It also changes indexing from 1–K to 0–K and adds a caveat about sometimes using K−1. Whether these represent procedural changes or pseudocode corrections remains unclear; the core components are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain WritingPrompts/RTP narrative prompts, WikiText-2 safe data, the HolisticBias SafeBank and the same English human-evaluation population. Revised sample counts do not introduce new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain the same base models, debiased checkpoints, self-correction and SGD/AdamW methods. Mistral was already evaluated in v2; newly cited ATTA and BA-LoRA are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 changes the reported safe-corpus size from 200 to 300 texts, and Appendix A changes precond_max from 384 to 500. Table 10's common human-evaluation subset changes from 21 to 20 prompt IDs. These are reported setting/sample revisions; reruns or new data collection are not established.

E4.justification: The optimizer, threshold, segmentation, multi-trigger and latency analyses are retained, as are the generated examples and plotted results. Figure 4's corrected description concerns an existing analysis rather than newly added evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same confidence-interval reporting, paired tests, DiD analysis, five-rater aggregation and Fleiss' kappa estimator. Revised kappa values and sample counts do not introduce a new statistical estimation or uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Prose PPL values are corrected to match unchanged Table 4: 17.204 to 19.427 for 64-token segments and 9.489 to 10.628 for 256-token segments. The stated PPL reduction becomes 37% instead of 40%. Table 10 revises agreement results, including overall kappa from 0.301 to 0.297, on the changed common subset; this is not a same-setting performance comparison.

T1.justification: Section 3.2.3 corrects the Fisher definition from the expected log-likelihood Hessian to its negative, repairing the sign underlying the KL quadratic approximation. Section 3.1 also expands the bias-score domain from outputs Y to prompts and outputs X union Y. The existing derivations and appendix assumptions otherwise remain.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same claims about OOD bias, triggered preconditioned adaptation, efficiency, generation quality and mitigation of forgetting. No main contribution is added or redefined.

C2.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendix L replace the interpretation of multi-trigger routing as having similar cost with doubled update cost, consistent with the existing 0.426 versus 0.846-second values. Figure 4's interpretation is corrected from sample-level safety/quality clusters to segment-level mean-bias trajectories. Limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A separates max_length=384 from the revised precond_max=500. Appendix P newly discloses a fluency attention check/filter, and Appendix J notes omitted update loops. The artifacts paragraph changes a planned release to a stated release at the same URL, although v2 already claimed code availability in its first-page footnote.

R1.justification: Section 2.3 adds Gao et al.'s ATTA and Chang et al.'s BA-LoRA to its discussion of adaptation and forgetting. Numerous other reference edits correct metadata or update matched publications. The paper's overall research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v4 corrects grammar and author-footnote symbols, cleans up references, renames Appendix F and adds brief clarifications. The section order and overall narrative are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 4 receives a corrected caption and appendix heading. Figure 8 uses the identical embedded diagram with reduced vertical scaling. Table 3 replaces nan with N/A, and Table 10 revises its exclusion placeholders and caption. No figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: Correcting the Fisher sign, Figure 4's description and prose values that contradicted Table 4 improves mathematical and reporting accuracy. Table 10 now uses 20 shared prompts, consistent with Table 5, and discloses filtering. These are useful but limited repairs; Algorithm 1 still leaves the implemented loss and segment count unclear.
